entry.title: SensorGuard-RV: Sensor-to-Register Data Protection for Resource-Constrained RISC-V Devices
entry.summary:
Embedded systems rely on sensor measurements that traverse a complex hardware-firmware stack (e.g. peripheral interfaces, communication buses, memory, and drivers) before reaching the applications that use them. At worst, an attacker with access to this path may successfully intercept, overwrite, fabricate, or replay readings.

entry.title: Zirah: A Post-Quantum True Random Number Generator Hardware Signer With an Avalanche Noise
entry.summary:
Zirah is a hardware signer built around an STM32F407 microcontroller, and its purpose is to find out, on inexpensive hardware, where a post-quantum signing key is exposed and what actually protects it. The device draws every random bit from a reverse-biased 2N3904 junction in avalanche breakdown, amplified by an LM358 and screened by SP 800-90B health tests, computes ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, hedged) on the STM32 with two-share arithmetic masking of the secret-key multiplications, and adds ECDSA P-256 from an ATECC608 secure element over the same digest, once a person has matched an eight-digit digest prefix on its OLED with the PC and pressed a button. A desktop application and a command-line tool drive the board and verify its output, and because only a 32-byte manifest digest reaches the device, it signs files of any type and size, returning signed copies for PDF, Office Open XML, ZIP, PNG and JPEG files and detached records for every other format.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #post-quantum

entry.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: SoK: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Integration in Software Development: Approaches, Gaps, and Future Directions
entry.summary:
Standardised post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is critical for protecting software systems against future quantum threats, but standardised algorithms alone do not provide a pathway for their secure integration into software. This paper presents a Systematisation of Knowledge (SoK) of PQC integration in software development, synthesising existing approaches across implementation, migration, and developer education. We analyse these approaches against NIST PQC standards and PQC migration guidance, software development lifecycle coverage, cybersecurity practices, deployment maturity, and testing and evaluation evidence.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #software-architecture #cryptography

entry.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
entry.summary:
Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task. Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #agents

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Correction of parameters in ``Computing Optimal Ate Pairings on Elliptic Curves with Embedding Degree 9, 15 and 27''
entry.summary:
We correct two errors in Section~8 of the above-mentioned paper concerning the seed parameters proposed for BLS27 elliptic curves (embedding degree $k=27$) at the 256-bit and 192-bit security levels. In both instances, the disclosed seeds produce a composite $r(x)$, violating the primality condition essential for constructing pairing-friendly curves. Additionally, for the 192-bit seed, the characteristic $p(x)$ is also composite.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory

entry.title: Radical 3-isogenies for the ideal class group actions on $(2, \varepsilon)$-structures
entry.summary:
Chenu and Smith introduced the notion of $(d,\varepsilon)$-structures, pairs consisting of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ and an isogeny of degree $d$ from the curve to its Galois conjugate, and defined an ideal class group action on supersingular $(d,\varepsilon)$-structures, inherited from the action on oriented supersingular elliptic curves. They also outlined extensions of the CSIDH key exchange and of the Delfs–Galbraith algorithm for the supersingular isogeny problem. In particular, they suggested that the latter, called the generalized Delfs–Galbraith algorithm, may be faster than the original one by a constant factor for small $d$, provided that the class group action on $(d,\varepsilon)$-structures can be evaluated efficiently.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory

entry.title: A proof of P≠NP (New symmetric encryption algorithm against any linear attacks and differential attacks)
entry.summary:
P vs NP problem is the most important unresolved problem in the field of computational complexity. Its impact has penetrated into all aspects of algorithm design, especially in the field of cryptography. The security of cryptographic algorithms based on short keys depends on whether P is equal to NP.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Repeated Masks, Predictable Splices: Breaking AESpolyW and Its AEAD Applications
entry.summary:
AESpolyW, presented at the 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, is a wide-block encryption mode that preserves the length of each message. Its design lets operations of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) overlap with hash computations based on polynomial evaluation. Our attacks splice ciphertexts by copying blocks from one ciphertext to the same positions in another.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: BAKSHEESH: Similar Yet Different From GIFT. We propose a lightweight block cipher named BAKSHEESH, which follows up on the popular cipher GIFT-128 (CHES'17).
entry.summary:
We propose a lightweight block cipher named BAKSHEESH, which follows up on the popular cipher GIFT-128 (CHES'17). BAKSHEESH runs for 35 rounds, which is 12.50 percent smaller compared to GIFT-128 (runs for 40 rounds) while maintaining the same security claims against the classical attacks. The crux of BAKSHEESH is to use a 4-bit SBox that has a non-trivial Linear Structure (LS).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
